caption:
"We do not throttle reach of AI content just for being AI content." That's Adam Mosseri, Instagram's head, in an AMA on October 16, 2026.

So the fear that using AI anywhere in your process quietly kills your reach is not true, and it has been costing people real time — hiding the tools they use, rewriting captions by hand to sound less "AI", avoiding editors that would make the work better.

What Instagram does want is the label. It is building more AI labels and pushing creators to tag AI content themselves, and in May 2026 it added an "AI Creator" label for accounts that regularly use AI tools. For brands in the EU this is becoming a legal question, not just a ranking one.

The honest read: the model is disclosure, not punishment. Undisclosed is the risk. Disclosed is fine.

Which means the question was never "will AI hurt my reach". It's whether the thing you made is worth watching.
